name: Layer42

profile.address: 3080, Raymond Street, Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, 95054
profile.reading:
The building at 3080 Raymond Street in Santa Clara, California carries the name Layer42 in this record, but the company that name refers to has not operated the building under its own brand for close to a decade. Layer42 Networks was founded in 1999 as a Silicon Valley business-to-business connectivity and colocation provider, eventually running about 70,000 square feet of data center space across sites in Santa Clara and Mountain View and serving roughly 150 customers, including well-known names like Dropbox, Square, and Barracuda Networks. On September 11, 2015, regional broadband and business-services provider Wave Broadband acquired Layer42 Networks outright and rebranded the unit "Layer42 by Wave," keeping Layer42's former CEO on as a senior data-center-services executive.

The Raymond Street building itself is documented in trade press coverage of a later transaction: at roughly 30,000 square feet with about 3 megawatts of total facility capacity, of which roughly 1.5 megawatts was available for colocation customers, it was one of the facilities Wave Broadband owned when Wave sold its Santa Clara data center business to VPLS in November 2021. VPLS rebranded the site "SV3" after the purchase. In other words, the chain of ownership runs from Layer42 Networks (pre-2015, independent), to Wave Broadband / "Layer42 by Wave" (2015-2021), to VPLS / SV3 (2021 onward) -- meaning the "Layer42" name attached to this address is a legacy brand from an ownership period that ended years ago rather than a description of who runs the building today.

For a small-to-midsize Silicon Valley colocation facility of this vintage and size, 3 megawatts of total capacity and 30,000 square feet puts it well below the scale of the hyperscale and wholesale campuses that have since come to dominate Santa Clara's data center market, more in line with a carrier-neutral facility built to serve network, cloud, and enterprise colocation customers needing proximity to Silicon Valley peering points rather than large single-tenant deployments. No additional detail on cooling architecture, redundancy tier, or current occupancy under VPLS/SV3 ownership was found in public reporting. Readers researching this address for current operational status should treat "Layer42" as a historical name rather than the facility's present operator.

reading: Layer42 Networks is an IP transit and network service provider operating its own Autonomous System, AS8121, rather than owning and leasing out data center real estate. The company maintains network presence in 28 data centers across the United States, with heavy concentration in the San Francisco Bay Area, including San Francisco, San Jose, Santa Clara, Palo Alto, Sunnyvale, and Milpitas, alongside points of presence in Los Angeles, Secaucus in New Jersey, Ashburn in Virginia, Seattle, Chicago, and New York. Layer42 operates as a network tenant and connectivity partner inside facilities owned by other operators, including Equinix, CoreSite, EdgeConneX, Evocative, and Lumen, several of which already appear as building owners elsewhere in this registry. This means the California facility recorded under Layer42's name in this registry most likely represents one of these colocated network points of presence, such as a Mountain View location referenced in third-party directories, rather than a Layer42-owned or operated building. Layer42's own materials did not publish a headquarters city, founding year, or ownership structure as of the research date, consistent with a network operator whose public presence is built around its connectivity product and peering relationships rather than corporate profile marketing.
